questions.stem: What is the digital root of a multiple of 9?
questions.solution: The digital root of a multiple of 9 is always 9. This is because the sum of the digits of any multiple of 9 is also a multiple of 9, and repeating the process gives 9. The other options are incorrect because they do not match the known property of multiples of 9.

hi.critique: The Hindi translation accurately reflects the English question and solution, with appropriate mathematical terminology used.

questions.stem: What is the digital root of a number that is exactly divisible by 9?
questions.solution: The digital root of a number exactly divisible by 9 is 9 because the digital root is the iterative sum of its digits until a single digit remains, and any multiple of 9 will reduce to 9. Choosing 1 would be incorrect because it does not result from summing the digits of a multiple of 9. Choosing 0 would be incorrect because no non-zero multiple of 9 has a digital root of 0. Choosing 3 would be incorrect because it does not correspond to the digital root of any number divisible by 9.

questions.stem: Which of the following expressions will always result in an even number?
questions.solution: The expression 2a + 2b will always result in an even number because both 2a and 2b are even numbers for any integer values of a and b. Adding two even numbers results in an even number. The other options may result in odd numbers depending on the values of the variables. For example, 43 + 37 is even, but 13k – 5k could be odd if k is odd, and 3g + 5h could be odd if both g and h are odd.

hi.critique: The Hindi translation is accurate, maintains the same meaning, and uses appropriate mathematical terminology.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of an algebraic expression that always results in an even number?
questions.solution: The expression 3n + 2 always results in an even number. This is because 3n is either even or odd, and adding 2 (an even number) to it keeps the result even. The other expressions can result in both even and odd numbers, depending on the value of n.

questions.stem: The sum of four consecutive numbers is 34. What are these numbers?
questions.solution: The sum of four consecutive numbers can be written as x + (x + 1) + (x + 2) + (x + 3) = 4x + 6. Setting this equal to 34 gives x = 7. Therefore, the numbers are 7, 8, 9, and 10. The other options do not satisfy the equation 4x + 6 = 34.

hi.stem: चार क्रमागत संख्याओं का योग 34 है। ये संख्याएँ क्या हैं?
hi.solution: चार क्रमागत संख्याओं का योग x + (x + 1) + (x + 2) + (x + 3) = 4x + 6 लिखा जा सकता है। इसे 34 के बराबर रखने पर x = 7 प्राप्त होता है। अतः संख्याएँ 7, 8, 9 और 10 हैं। अन्य विकल्प 4x + 6 = 34 के समीकरण को संतुष्ट नहीं करते।
hi.critique: The translation is accurate, maintains the original meaning, and uses appropriate Hindi mathematical terminology.

questions.stem: If the digital root of an 8-digit number is 5, what will be the digital root of 10 more than that number?
questions.solution: The digital root of a number increases by 1 when 10 is added to it. So, if the digital root is 5, adding 10 will make the digital root 6. Choosing 5 is incorrect because it assumes the digital root does not change. Choosing 15 is incorrect because it is not a valid digital root (digital roots are between 1 and 9). Choosing 1 is incorrect because it does not follow the rule of adding 1 to the digital root when 10 is added.

questions.stem: Which of the following is always true when a number is divisible by 8?
choices: The number is also divisible by 6
The number is also divisible by 12
The number is also divisible by 2
The number is also divisible by 10
questions.solution: If a number is divisible by 8, it is also divisible by 2 because 8 is a multiple of 2. The number may or may not be divisible by 6 or 12, depending on its value. Similarly, it may not be divisible by 10. Hence, the only statement that is always true is that the number is divisible by 2.

hi.stem: कौन-सा कथन हमेशा सत्य होता है जब कोई संख्या 8 से विभाज्य होती है?

questions.stem: Which of the following expressions correctly represents numbers that are 3 more than a multiple of 5?
questions.solution: The correct expression is 5k + 3 because it represents numbers that are 3 more than a multiple of 5. When you add 3 to a multiple of 5, such as 5k, you get exactly this form. The other options do not match this condition: 3k + 5 is not a multiple of 5 plus 3, 5k - 2 is 2 less than a multiple of 5, and 5k + 2 is 2 more than a multiple of 5.

hi.solution: सही व्यंजक 5k + 3 है क्योंकि यह 5 के गुणज से 3 अधिक संख्याओं को दर्शाता है। जब आप 5k के गुणज में 3 जोड़ते हैं, तो आपको ठीक इस रूप में परिणाम मिलता है। अन्य विकल्प इस स्थिति के अनुरूप नहीं हैं: 3k + 5, 5 के गुणज में 3 जोड़ने के बराबर नहीं है, 5k - 2, 5 के गुणज से 2 कम है, और 5k + 2, 5 के गुणज से 2 अधिक है।

questions.stem: What is the smallest number that leaves a remainder of 2 when divided by 3, a remainder of 3 when divided by 4, and a remainder of 4 when divided by 5?
questions.solution: The number must be one less than a multiple of 3, 4, and 5. The LCM of 3, 4, and 5 is 60, so the smallest such number is 60 − 1 = 59. The other options are either not one less than a multiple of all three numbers or are not the smallest.

questions.stem: If a number has a digital root of 3, what is the remainder when the number is divided by 9?
questions.solution: The remainder when a number is divided by 9 is the same as its digital root, unless the digital root is 9, in which case the remainder is 0. So, if the digital root is 3, the remainder will also be 3. Choosing 0 is incorrect because it applies to numbers with a digital root of 9. Choosing 6 or 9 is incorrect because it does not match the rule for a digital root of 3.

questions.stem: Which of the following algebraic expressions can represent all numbers that leave a remainder of 3 when divided by 5?
questions.solution: The expression 5n + 3 represents all numbers that leave a remainder of 3 when divided by 5. questions.stem: If a number is a multiple of 11, and when doubled, it is also a multiple of 11, which of the following is the correct explanation?
choices: Doubling a multiple of 11 does not change its divisibility by 11.
Doubling a multiple of 11 makes it not divisible by 11.

questions.solution: If a number is a multiple of 11, it can be expressed as 11 times some integer. When doubled, it becomes 22 times that integer, which is still divisible by 11. questions.stem: If a number is divisible by both 9 and 4, which of the following must it also be divisible by?
questions.solution: If a number is divisible by both 9 and 4, it must be divisible by their least common multiple, which is 36. This is because 9 and 4 have no common factors other than 1, so their LCM is 9 × 4 = 36. The number may or may not be divisible by 12, 16, or 18, depending on its value, but it must be divisible by 36.
